layers.note: The dominant bunchgrass of the south Puget Sound prairies and oak savannas.

moisture.note: Dry, well-drained prairie soils on glacial outwash.

heat_load.note: Warm, sunny ground; favours slopes facing south and west.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 1,500 m in western Washington; the upper limits are loose.

shade_tolerance.note: Needs full sun; disappears under trees.

coldest_c.note: Across its range (see the provenance note), coldest-month means from about −3 °C, gone by −8 °C, up to about 13 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −22 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −30 °C.

warmest_c.note: Warm, dry summers: warmest-month means from about 15.5 to 27 °C, gone below 13 °C and above 30.5 °C.

degree_days_0.note: A long warm season: about 3,100 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 2,400.

degree_days_5.note: About 1,600 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 1,100: it stays in warm lowlands and on the lower slopes.

moisture_index.note: Summer drought borne: a moisture index from about 0.32 (gone by 0.2), dry savanna and prairie climates included.

summer_rain.note: A Mediterranean-type climate: its range lies where at most about 0.2 of the year's precipitation falls in summer, gone by 0.35.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Roemer's fescue grows in prairies and oak savanna from Vancouver Island to north-west California (FEIS, the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
